title: Compile only the wasmparser and wasm-encoder features the Wasm cell facade uses
goal: Reduce the CPU work of the cold `cargo build -p susi` on Linux x86_64 (what costs wall time when the laptop is loaded) without changing behaviour: susi-vendor-wasmtime uses only wasmparser's core-module reader and wasm-encoder's core-module encoder to cap a cell's memory section, so their default validator, component model, serde and hash-collection features are not compiled.

results.change: crates/susi-vendor-wasmtime/Cargo.toml: wasmparser 0.259 and wasm-encoder 0.259 with default-features = false, features = ["std"]. cell.rs uses Parser, Payload, Encoding and MemorySectionReader from wasmparser and Module, RawSection, MemorySection, MemoryType from wasm-encoder; the version header (and so the refusal of WASM components as cells) is parsed without the component-model feature (wasmparser 0.259 src/parser.rs, State::Header). Cargo.lock drops ahash, getrandom 0.3.4, r-efi, wasip2 and wit-bindgen.
results.measurement_method: Alternated fully cold `cargo build -p susi --offline --locked --timings` into empty target directories, base worktree at 871425ffa (T-CORECUT-1) then this change, three pairs back to back; load average and rustc count recorded before each run.

verification.cargo test -p susi-daemon --lib crown: 7 passed (the crown sandbox probes run through the memory-capping parser with the production feature set; the daemon has no wat dev-dependency)

limitations: Whole-build wall time is inside this host's load noise and is not claimed; the measured effect is wasmparser's own compile time (about 45% lower) and 10 fewer units.

susi-vendor-wasmtime's own test binary still compiles the full features through its `wat` dev-dependency (Cargo unifies dev-dependency features in test builds), so its tests do not run the trimmed feature set; the daemon's crown tests do.

provenance.agent: corecut (Cursor subagent, CachyOS Linux x86_64, CEO laptop)
